pr_body:
Closes #8215 

Changes:
* Add `to_string` to the temporal namespace. `strftime` is now an alias for this method - we give users the option to use the familiar `strftime`, but internally we use the more readable `to_string`.
* Update references, docstrings, etc.

I'm planning to make the `format` parameter optional, and move the logic for determining a default format from `cast` to this method, and have `cast` call this method. But I'll do that refactor in another PR.
pr_comments: I believe we still miss a docs entry (maybe I missed it).

> I believe we still miss a docs entry (maybe I missed it).

Oops, I missed that one. Added now.

_(I'd swear the CI used to fail when there were undocumented methods...)_
Re-added the alias on the ChunkedArray level - I guess these are public and might be used also. That should cover any concerns.
@ritchie46 I think this can be merged - or do you have any doubts?
@ritchie46 gentle ping :) As I said, if you have any doubts, I don't mind addressing them.
Seems good. Architecture seems the same. As long as `strftime` is still available on all levels, feel free to merge. :)
All right, then I'm pressing the green button :)

issue_context.title: Rename `str.strptime`/`dt.strftime` methods
issue_context.body:
These names are well-established historically, but definitely do not follow our naming conventions.

I would suggest:
* `str.strptime` -> `str.to_timestamp`
* `dt.strftime` -> `dt.to_string`



There might be better names - suggestions?
comments:
If we went this route, I think `strptime` should be split into two functions:

* `str.strptime(pl.Date, fmt)` -> `.str.to_date()`
* `str.strptime(pl.Datetime, fmt)` -> `.str.to_datetime()`.

I always forget to put in the dtype.

I really like that idea - makes things very explicit.

If we do keep it as one method, we should probably try to infer the dtype from the given format.
Because of there historical significance, I'd like to keep them, but I'd be ok with adding aliases for them that are better in line with our naming conventions.

in this context I would also very much welcome a
- `str.to_duration` and/or
- `str.strptime(pl.Duration, fmt)`

as suggested here #7397.

I occasionally work with durations (call data, experiments, ...) which are usually in the format H:MM:SS where the hours can also be >24 (or negative) (123:45:00; -1:23:00).

Unfortunately, I currently always switch to pandas for this because of the very practical `pd.to_timedelta` method (https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/stable/reference/api/pandas.to_timedelta.html).

Agreed @JulianCologne. All right, so then we'll keep the existing methods, and add the following aliases:

* `str.to_date`
* `str.to_time`
* `str.to_datetime`
* `str.to_duration` _(requires expanding current_ `strptime` _functionality)_
* `dt.to_string`

@ritchie46 Do you want these aliases under Rust too? Or only for Python users?

Also pinging datetime-overlord @MarcoGorelli to see if he has an opinion 😄

> @ritchie46 Do you want these aliases under Rust too? Or only for Python users?

On rust on the expressions. let's try to keep that 1:1. :)

> Also pinging datetime-overlord @MarcoGorelli to see if he has an opinion 😄

😄 cheers - well, thinking with my "coming from pandas" hat on, I think `str.to_datetime` would be a nice and clear addition! Likewise for the others
This issue is now completed - for the implementation of `dt.to_duration`, please refer to issue https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/7397.

review_comments: Which then makes these changes unneeded.

I thought it would be nice to use the more readable / more ideally named version internally, and keep `strftime` for Polars users who have familiarity with that name.

But indeed, technically we can keep using `strftime` here if we keep those methods on the chunked arrays.

RUST SIDE:

Do we now have `strftime` and `to_string` as expression? I think we should keep both on the expression side to keep consistency with python. 

In the lower level implementation, I think it's fine to only keep `to_string`.

> RUST SIDE:
> 
> Do we now have `strftime` and `to_string` as expression? I think we should keep both on the expression side to keep consistency with python.

We do! `DateLikeNameSpace` has both `to_string` and `strftime` implemented.

And for Series, `TemporalMethods` also has both. So that should cover it.

Why are these renamed? 

Shouldn't we just be able to add 2 aliases?

We can! I had it like that initially, but aren't these always accessed through the namespace? In that case, we only need the alias on the namespace level (which is how it is now).

But if these methods on the chunked array are called directly by users then we should keep the `strftime` method.

(this really shows my inexperience with the Rust side... just tell me what to do here!)

@ritchie46 Could you get back to me on this one? I will update the PR accordingly.

The way I see it, `strftime` is still available on the Expr namespace and on Series, so that should be enough.
